title: Standing thoracic kyphosis and extension range (radiographic Cobb)
condition: healthy, standing (arms elevated 70 deg on support for neutral), maximal thoracic extension with arms fully elevated

quantity.name: thoracic kyphosis and range of extension
quantity.definition: Cobb angle T3-T11; range = neutral kyphosis minus kyphosis at extreme extension

source.authors: Edmondston SJ, Christensen MM, Keller S, Steigen LB, Barclay L
source.sample: 14 asymptomatic male university staff/students, no thoracolumbar scoliosis, chronic respiratory disorder or recent spinal pain

protocol.summary: Neutral and end-range extension thoracic kyphosis in standing; radiographic and photographic methods on the same subjects (r = 0.69 between methods).
how_to_use: Use ~12 deg (SD 9) as the standing thoracic extension range beyond neutral kyphosis; distribute it over T3-T11 (radiograph) or T1-T12.
Larger neutral kyphosis -> larger extension range (r = 0.71): scale the range with the subject's kyphosis if known.
End-range extension posture here includes full arm elevation and backward reach.

measurement.device: lateral thoracic digital radiographs (Shimadzu RADspeed / AGFA CR), Cobb angle T3 superior endplate to T11 inferior endplate
measurement.task: neutral standing and maximal active thoracic extension (reach up and bend backward)

extraction.check_notes: Table 2 values re-read; range means agree with abstract (12.0 ± 8.9 radiograph, 12.4 ± 4.1 photograph; abstract rounds ranges to 0-26 and 8-23 deg).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
